model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two different models, labeled "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," across a range of sparsity rates from 10% to 80%. The x-axis represents the sparsity rate, with values marked at 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%. The y-axis, labeled "Perplexity," is on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000). For each sparsity rate, two bars are shown: a blue bar for "Per-Output" and an orange bar for "Per-Layer." The data reveals that as the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity for both models generally increases. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 40%), the perplexity for both models is low, with the "Per-Output" model showing a slightly lower perplexity than the "Per-Layer" model. At 50% sparsity, the perplexity for both models increases to approximately 10. At 60% sparsity, the perplexity for both models is around 10, with the "Per-Output" model having a slightly lower value. At 70% sparsity, the perplexity for the "Per-Output" model is approximately 15, while for the "Per-Layer" model, it is around 50. At 80% sparsity, the perplexity for the "Per-Output" model is approximately 500, and for the "Per-Layer" model, it is approximately 1000, indicating a significant increase in perplexity for both models as sparsity increases, with the "Per-Layer" model showing a more pronounced increase.
